diagnostic_evidence.quote: Then the latter argument follows trivially since $L(h, \alpha) = L$ if $U^\varepsilon_{h, \alpha} \subseteq U^\varepsilon$

issues.failure_explanation: U^eps_{h,alpha} contains every point x + t h Y_h(x), t in [0,1]. The proof only shows that each segment S_k lies in the larger set U^{eps+Delta} and that the endpoint satisfies V(x_{k+1}) <= eps. It never shows V <= eps at intermediate points, so the asserted inclusion U^eps_{h,beta/h} ⊆ U^eps is unproved. The 'Moreover' optimality clause relies on exactly this inclusion through L(h,alpha) = L.

failure_location.quote: $U^\varepsilon_{h, \frac{\beta}{h}} \subseteq U^\varepsilon$ and thus $V^{-1}([0, \varepsilon])$ is positive invariant

issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Apply (eq:V_segment1) at every t in [0,1] instead of only t = 1. Since 1 - t beta Lbar/2 >= 1 - beta Lbar/2 and t <= 1, the same step-size restrictions give V(x + t h Y_h(x)) <= eps for all t, hence the inclusion.
issues.overall_effect: The inclusion claim, and the identification L(h,alpha) = L used to call alpha = 1/(hL) the minimiser of the bound, are unsupported as written. Positive invariance of V^{-1}([0,eps]) itself is proved.
issues.title: Claimed inclusion of the whole Euler-segment set in U^eps is not proved
issues.why_classification: A local re-use of the existing estimate with the same h_0 suffices, and all claims survive.

diagnostic_evidence.quote: We note that for $h < \frac{1}{2}h_0(\varepsilon')$, one can further shrink $\varepsilon'$ to maintain the inequality.
there exists $T_{\mathrm{update}}>0$ and $h_0 > 0$ such that for all $h \in (0, h_0)$

issues.failure_explanation: The tube bound grows like (T_update/h) * eps~^q. For fixed eps~ it diverges as h -> 0. To control it the proof needs a lower bound h_0(eps) >= K eps^theta with K uniform over gain updates. An O(eps^theta) upper bound does not imply that eps'^q/h_0(eps') stays bounded. The estimate is carried out only at the single step size h = h_0(eps~)/2. The claimed 'for all h in (0,h_0)' rests on an unspecified re-choice of the invariant level ('further shrink eps''), with the contradiction argument mixing eps~ and eps'. Uniformity of the constants (mu, theta, B_{x_k} <= max{L,H_min}) is never verified.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: From the explicit step-size bounds in the proof of thm:optimal_a with local Hessian bound c B_{x_k} <= c max{L,H_min}, prove h_0(eps) >= K eps^theta with uniform K. For each h, choose the level eps~(h) with h comparable to h_0(eps~(h)). Choose T_update small in terms of K, Gamma, Cbar, F_eps, H_min and c. Redo the block induction with this single h-dependent level, counting all tau terms in the displacement sum.
issues.overall_effect: The positive-invariance guarantee for Algorithm 2 with a time-based update period is not established for all small h as stated. The cost/accuracy claims based on it lack a proof.
issues.title: Step-size/level coupling in the update-period theorem rests on a wrong-direction bound and is shown for only one h
issues.why_classification: The conclusion survives, but the quantifier structure of the proof must be rebuilt with a new contained lemma (uniform lower bound on h_0).

diagnostic_evidence.quote: The fixed gain choice $\alpha=\tfrac{1}{hL}$ diverges only at the largest step $h = 10^{-1}$
Over the entire tested range of $h$, the adaptive gain feedback integrator keeps the error bounded.
In the Kepler problem, they also outperformed the Störmer-Verlet benchmark across the entire tested step sizes.

issues.failure_explanation: The paper claims both the adaptive and fixed-gain schemes give the highest accuracy over the whole tested range, and the conclusion says both outperform Störmer–Verlet at every tested step. Yet the paper reports that the fixed-gain scheme diverges at h = 10^{-1} while the adaptive scheme stays bounded. At that step the fixed-gain scheme therefore cannot be among the most accurate, nor shown to beat the benchmark.

failure_location.quote: adaptive gain and the fixed gain $\alpha=\tfrac{1}{hL}$ feedback integrators deliver the highest accuracy among all schemes across the tested range of $h$

issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Restrict the claims to the step sizes where the fixed-gain scheme stays bounded (h < 10^{-1}), or attribute full-range superiority only to the adaptive scheme.
issues.overall_effect: The advertised empirical superiority of the fixed-gain rule over the full tested range in the Kepler test, as restated in the conclusion, is not supported by the reported results.
issues.title: Kepler accuracy claims contradict the reported divergence of the fixed-gain scheme
issues.why_classification: Rewording the prose fixes it; no theoretical result is affected.
